Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.

# Intake Brief: Follow-on-Steam incentive — unlock a bundled free game in the Steam launcher

## Problem statement

The upcoming Steam release of the Tableau Card Engine launcher (Electron) needs a growth mechanic: when a player follows the game/developer on Steam, they receive one of the bundled example games for free. The mechanic must feel seamless — the Steam store page opens automatically (player already logged in), they follow, and the launcher detects the follow and unlocks the bonus game.

## Users

- **Steam players** — get a free game as an incentive to follow the TCE Steam presence; discover the engine's games.
- **TCE developers/publisher** — grow Steam following/wishlists and reward engaged players without manual key distribution.

**User stories:**
- As a Steam player, I want to click "Follow us on Steam" in the launcher and have the store page open automatically (already logged in), so following takes one click.
- As a Steam player, I want the bonus game to unlock in my launcher once I've followed, so I can play it immediately.
- As a publisher, I want the free-game unlock to be delivered through the existing bundled-content/DLC architecture, so no manual key handling is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The launcher shows a "Follow us on Steam" call-to-action (e.g. a small panel/button) that opens the game's Steam store page in the Steam client/overlay via Steamworks (player is already logged in — no browser login prompt).
2. After the player follows, the launcher detects the follow via Steamworks and unlocks the designated bonus game (one of the existing example games) in the launcher's game list; verified by an end-to-end check with a real Steam account (manual QA) and, where feasible, a mocked Steamworks session in automated tests.
3. The unlock persists across launches (player who followed once keeps the game; no re-verification prompt on every boot).
4. The bonus game is delivered as part of the bundled-content architecture (locked by default) so no separate download is needed; the unlock mechanism is game-agnostic (works for whichever game is designated as the bonus).
5. If the Steam client/Steamworks is unavailable (e.g. dev environment, non-Steam launch), the launcher must not crash: the CTA degrades gracefully (hidden or "follow via browser" fallback) and the web app remains fully functional.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test`) and `npm run build` must succeed (quality gate).

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Electron** launcher per CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW; this feature integrates Steamworks SDK into that launcher (explicitly deferred scope of the launcher item — this item introduces it).
- **Bonus game is bundled** (answer to intake Q: "a game currently in the example games", delivered via the bundled/subset content in the launcher, unlocked in place) — not a separate download.
- **Steam store page via Steamworks** (intake Q3): the CTA opens the store page in the Steam client; follow detection must use the Steamworks SDK and/or Steam Web API.
- **Licensing:** all code MIT-compatible; no proprietary or copyleft dependencies.
- **Quality gates:** `npm test` and `npm run build` must pass before pushing (project policy).
- **Doc-update policy:** infra/tooling changes require `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `AGENTS.md` updates (or a tracked child work item).
- **Game-agnostic:** the unlock logic must not hard-code the specific bonus game title (the designated game is a business decision, see Appendix).

## Existing state

- Launcher item CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW (intake_complete) delivers the Electron binary that boots the Vite web app; scope explicitly defers Steamworks SDK integration ("No Steamworks SDK integration in v1. The launcher must not require Steam to run locally during development.").
- Launcher content-loading is designed so Steam DLC directories can be read (option a) with structure permitting later Steamworks-managed paths (option b) without a rewrite — the follow-unlock must slot into this abstraction.
- The web app (Game Selector) currently lists all example games; the launcher will bundle a subset.
- No Steamworks SDK, Steam app ID, or Steam-related code exists in the repo today.

## Desired change

1. Add Steamworks SDK integration to the Electron launcher (init/restart-app-if-needed, Steam app ID bootstrap), keeping the launcher runnable without Steam during development.
2. Add a "Follow us on Steam" CTA (in launcher UI, e.g. Game Selector screen or settings) that opens the game's Steam store page in the Steam client — candidate mechanisms: `SteamFriends()->ActivateGameOverlayToStore(appId, ...)` in the Steamworks SDK, or `steam://openurl`/`steam://store/<appid>` external URL from Electron.
3. Detect the follow and unlock the bonus game. **Research required:** Steam's client SDK has no direct "user follows this game's store page" call; candidates to verify during implementation:
   - `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing(<developer account steamID>)` — client-side check that the user follows the *developer/publisher account* (works without a backend).
   - Steam Web API (`IPlayerService` family, e.g. followed-games queries) — verifies game-page follows but needs a server component and publisher API key.
   - Whichever mechanism is chosen must be verified against the actual Steam account model (game-page follow vs developer-account follow) before committing.
4. Unlock persistence: store a local unlock flag (or Steam-follow state) so the player isn't re-prompted; re-check on demand (e.g. "Refresh" or on follow confirmation).
5. Graceful degradation when Steam/Steamworks is absent: CTA hidden or browser fallback; web app unaffected.
6. Tests + docs: mock Steamworks session for automated unlock-logic tests where feasible; manual end-to-end QA with a real Steam account documented in the test plan.

## Key Files

- `electron/main.ts` (new) — Steamworks init, Steam app ID bootstrap, store-page open handler, follow-check orchestration.
- `electron/steam-follow.ts` (new) — follow detection + unlock persistence logic (game-agnostic), behind a small interface so the web renderer doesn't depend on the Steam SDK directly.
- `electron/preload.ts` (new) — expose a minimal follow/unlock API to the renderer via context bridge.
- `src/ui/` or launcher UI module — "Follow us on Steam" CTA component (SLL-compliant placement), unlock state display.
- `package.json` — Steamworks SDK dependency (or native module) and scripts; electron-builder config for the Steam distribution.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `README.md`, `RELEASE.md` — document the Steamworks build/QA workflow.
- `AGENTS.md` — note new scripts/requirements if tooling changes.
- `tests/` — unit tests for unlock/persistence logic with a mocked follow source; manual E2E test plan for real-Steam verification.

## Related work

- **CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW – Electron launcher for a Steam-ready binary release** (open, intake_complete) — prerequisite: the launcher this feature extends. Its AC #4 (DLC/content-location architecture) must be honored; this feature introduces the deferred Steamworks scope.
- `docs/the-build/genre-research.md` — card-game genre research incl. Steam platform notes (context only).
- No other Steam/Steamworks work items exist (verified via `wl search steam`, `steamworks`, `DLC`).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** The Steam app (App ID) and developer/publisher Steam account exist outside this repo; this item integrates with them.
- **Assumption:** The designated bonus game is a business decision (TBD — see Appendix) and does not change the technical design (game-agnostic unlock).
- **Assumption:** Following is checked once (on CTA completion) and persisted locally; unfollow-after-unlock is not detected/penalised in v1 (anti-abuse is out of scope).
- **Risk (HIGH):** Steam's client SDK may not expose a reliable client-side "followed this game page" check. Mitigation: implementation begins with a short research spike (candidate APIs above); fallback is developer-account follow via `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing`, or a small web-API verification if acceptable. This may change the UX (e.g. follow developer account instead of game page) — confirm with user before committing to a fallback.
- **Risk:** Steamworks native module adds build complexity to electron-builder packaging and must not break non-Steam dev runs — mitigated by graceful-degradation AC (AC5).
- **Risk:** Electron + Steamworks native module (Steam SDK) packaging on Windows must be validated (steam_appid.txt, app id bootstrap, `SteamAPI_RestartAppIfNecessary`).
- **Scope-creep risk:** Steam overlay for achievements, wishlist prompts, key-distribution systems, and anti-abuse (unfollow detection) are out of scope; record as follow-up work items rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which game is being released on Steam? The TCE is an engine — are we releasing a specific game built on it (e.g., Main Street), or is this about the engine itself?" — Answer (user): "A launcher with a subset of the example games bundled and the ability to add more later (DLC)." Source: interactive reply. Implication: the Steam "release" is the launcher product (per CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW); this item is a mechanic in that launcher.
- Q2: "What's the 'free game' offer? When a player follows, they receive a free game — is that a specific existing game from the TCE catalog, a bonus game, or something else?" — Answer (user): "it will be a game currently in the example games." Source: interactive reply. The specific game title is **not yet chosen (OPEN QUESTION for the business)**; ACs are game-agnostic.
- Q3: "How does the Steam integration work: store page with follow-to-unlock via Steamworks API, manual key-claim flow, or something else?" — Answer (user): "Steam store page via Steamworks." Source: interactive reply.
- Q4: "What platform does the launcher target?" — Answer (user): "desktop (we will be using electron, another item covers this, add requirements there if necessary, see CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW)". Source: interactive reply. Decision: Electron stack already scoped in CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW; no requirements added to that item (its scope explicitly defers Steamworks — this feature introduces it and is linked as dependent).
- Q5: "What does 'follow us on Steam' mean technically? Steam has no direct follow webhook..." (options: web flow with in-game store open + API check; code redemption; community group) — Answer (user): "I have played a game that automatically opened the steam store page, I was already logged in and I was following the page. I don't know how they did it, but that's what I want." Source: interactive reply. This is the target UX; the exact Steamworks mechanism is a research spike for implementation (see Risks). Likely components: `ActivateGameOverlayToStore` (or `steam://store/<appid>`) to open the page + a follow-state check.
- OPEN QUESTION: Which example game is the designated free follow-bonus? (business decision; doesn't block technical design — AC4 is game-agnostic.)
- OPEN QUESTION: Follow verification mechanism — game-page follow (needs Steam Web API / backend) vs developer-account follow (`ISteamFriends::IsFollowing`, client-side). Must be researched and confirmed with user before implementation commits to a fallback.

## Related work (automated find-related report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MSI4IP6A000N7YF** – Coloretto: align player collections (hands) regardless of name/score length (completed) — *weak match (generic keyword overlap; unrelated game feature)*.
- **CG-0MQH81RIS0017K94** – Coloretto Phaser scene (completed) — *weak match (generic keyword overlap; unrelated)*.
- **CG-0MROXIJZ3004VGUI** – GymTokenPileView: card-back pile shows 'not found' texture (completed) — *weak match (generic keyword overlap; unrelated)*.

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-...` — the draft itself (self-match).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (+ a worktree copy) — generic terms (game, feature, store); context only, no Steam-specific content.

> Note: The genuinely related item **CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW** (Electron launcher) is covered in the manual Related work section above.

# Intake Brief: Challenges as achievements — sync in-game challenges to Steam achievements

## Problem statement

The engine's challenge system (per-run meta-goals, e.g. Main Street's "Foodie Row") is conceptually a form of achievement. Once the Steam version exists (Electron launcher with Steamworks), challenge completions should sync to Steam achievements so players earn persistent, account-level recognition visible on their Steam profile and in the overlay.

## Users

- **Steam players** — earn Steam achievements for completing in-game challenges; see progress on their Steam profile.
- **TCE developers/publisher** — an engine-generic achievement layer so any game can map its challenges to Steam achievements without writing Steam SDK code.

**User stories:**
- As a Steam player, I want the challenges I complete in Main Street (and future games) to appear as Steam achievements, so my progress is recognised beyond the run itself.
- As a TCE developer, I want a game-agnostic achievement layer in the engine, so adding achievements to a new game is declarative (challenge → achievement mapping) with no Steam SDK code in the game.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. An **engine-generic achievement layer** exists in the core engine (extending the existing generic `ChallengeSystem` model): games define achievement definitions (id, title, description, hidden flag) and map challenge completions to achievements. This layer is pure engine code with no Steam dependency (works headless / in the web build).
2. When a challenge is completed inside the Steam launcher, the mapped Steam achievement is unlocked via Steamworks (`ISteamUserStats::SetAchievement` + `StoreStats`); verified by automated tests with a mocked Steamworks session and a documented manual E2E check with a real Steam account.
3. Steam sync is **idempotent and offline-safe**: unlocked achievements persist locally, are re-synced to Steam when available, and the launcher never crashes when Steam/Steamworks is absent (graceful degradation, consistent with the follow-on-Steam feature CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC).
4. A single **achievement manifest** (game id ↔ achievement id ↔ Steam API name, hidden flag) is the source of truth and matches the static Steam store configuration; mismatch detection is documented.
5. **Main Street is the first consumer**: all 12 challenge templates (`MainStreetChallenges.ts`) are mapped to Steam achievements through the generic layer (no Steam SDK code in the game module).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test`) and `npm run build` must succeed (quality gate).

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Timing:** Steam sync is implemented only when the Steam version exists — blocked by the Electron launcher (CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW) and the Steamworks integration introduced by the follow-on-Steam incentive (CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC). The engine-generic achievement layer itself can be designed/built now; the Steam bridge lands with Steamworks.
- **Engine-generic (user decision):** no game-specific Steam code; games declare achievements via the generic layer; Main Street first.
- **Steam backend reality:** Steam achievements must be pre-defined on the Steam store backend with static API names (App ID + achievement list). The manifest must match that configuration; store setup itself lives outside this repo.
- **Licensing:** all code MIT-compatible; no proprietary or copyleft dependencies (Steamworks SDK usage follows the pattern set by CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC).
- **Quality gates:** `npm test` and `npm run build` must pass before pushing (project policy).
- **Doc-update policy:** infra/tooling changes require `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `AGENTS.md` updates (or a tracked child work item).

## Existing state

- `src/core-engine/ChallengeSystem.ts` — generic `ChallengeDefinition<TState>` / `ActiveChallengeRecord<TState>` interfaces plus generic selection/evaluation; game-agnostic by design ("M6 extraction" notes already anticipate reuse).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetChallenges.ts` — the only consumer: 12 challenge templates across 5 categories, per-run selection (`selectChallenges`), evaluation with completion callback that pushes to `state.challengesCompleted` and the activity log. Challenges are run-local and non-persistent.
- No achievements, no Steam SDK code, no Electron code in the repo today. Steamworks integration is being introduced by CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC into the launcher from CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW.
- CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC explicitly defers this scope: "Steam overlay for achievements, wishlist prompts, key-distribution systems, and anti-abuse (unfollow detection) are out of scope; record as follow-up work items rather than expanding this item."

## Desired change

1. Add an **achievement concept to the core engine** (new module, e.g. `src/core-engine/AchievementSystem.ts`, or an extension of `ChallengeSystem`): achievement definitions, a completion-event surface, and a persistence-agnostic "unlock" registry that the web build can use without Steam.
2. Define the **achievement manifest** for the launcher (`electron/steam-achievements.ts`): game/achievement ids ↔ Steam API names + hidden flags, documented to match the Steam store backend config.
3. Add the **Steam bridge** in the Electron main process: renderer reports achievement-unlocked events via preload/IPC; main process calls Steamworks `SetAchievement`/`StoreStats`; local persistence of unlocked ids with later re-sync; graceful degradation without Steam.
4. **Wire Main Street** as the first consumer: a declarative mapping from the 12 challenge templates to Steam achievements, fired from the existing challenge-completion path.
5. Tests (mocked Steamworks session; headless unit tests for the engine layer) + documentation (README, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `AGENTS.md` as needed).

- `src/core-engine/AchievementSystem.ts` (new) — generic achievement definitions + unlock registry + completion-event surface (no Steam dependency).
- `src/core-engine/index.ts` — barrel exports for the new module.
- `electron/steam-achievements.ts` (new) — achievement manifest (ids ↔ Steam API names) + Steamworks sync bridge.
- `electron/main.ts`, `electron/preload.ts` — IPC surface for achievement-unlock events from the renderer.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetChallenges.ts` (or a new `MainStreetAchievements.ts`) — mapping of the 12 challenge templates to achievements.
- `tests/` — unit tests (engine layer, manifest matching) + mocked-Steamworks sync tests.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `README.md` — Steam achievements workflow documentation.

## Related work

- **CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC – Follow-on-Steam incentive: unlock a bundled free game in the Steam launcher** (open, intake_complete) — introduces Steamworks SDK integration into the Electron launcher; explicitly defers achievements as a follow-up; its Steamworks setup (init, app ID, mock strategy) is a prerequisite and pattern for this item.
- **CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW – Electron launcher for a Steam-ready binary release** (open, plan_complete) — the "Steam version"; provides the Electron main/preload and DLC content architecture this feature plugs into.
- **CG-0MSMGKVSS000ZEDL – Achievement give-aways: unlock three games when achievements are achieved** (open, idea) — separate item that consumes this item's achievement events as unlock triggers.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "Steam version" means the Electron launcher per CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW / CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC.
- **Assumption:** Steam achievements must be pre-defined on the Steamworks backend (static API names); the manifest must match that config — coordination with Steam store setup (outside repo) is required before release.

- **Risk:** Steamworks native module packaging complexity — reuse the approach validated by CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Steam cloud saves, non-binary stat tracking, trading cards, and wishlist prompts are out of scope; record as follow-up work items rather than expanding this item.

Source: interactive reply (2026-08-09). Implication: the layer is a core-engine module; Main Street is the first consumer.

Implication: implementation of the Steam bridge is gated on the launcher + Steamworks items; the engine abstraction is not.
- OPEN QUESTION: The exact Steam achievement list/API names for the store backend (business/backend decision outside the repo) — the manifest defines them in one place; the store config must match.

# Staff job-applicant specialization mechanic

## Problem statement

Main Street currently has a single staff mechanic: staff cards that go into the player's hand and passively expand hand capacity (`handSlotsAdded`). There is no in-game staff that is employed at a specific deployed business and grants that business a passive specialization buff. This item adds that new staff mechanic.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — wants more meaningful decisions when hiring staff: choosing where to place an applicant, weighing passive buffs, and taking on per-turn salary costs.
- **Game designer** — wants a reusable, deterministic staff-applicant mechanic that works with existing staff templates and can be extended with new applicant cards later.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Applicant trigger:** Each turn there is a per-turn chance that a staff member applies for work at one of the deployed businesses on the street. The chance is computed as `(reputation + income per turn)%`, capped at 15%. The applicant targets a deployed business that has a free employment slot (one staff slot per business level).
- **Passive specialization buff:** Each staff member grants a passive, always-on buff to the business at which they are employed. Skills are assigned from a specialization pool and are randomized **once per game** at game start, remaining locked for the full game; a staff member's skill is disconnected from its nominal job (e.g. a "Baker" can carry a "Town Gossip" skill). At a minimum the "Town Gossip" skill is implemented, firing the existing once-per-turn peek mechanic (see CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN).
- **Hire / decline flow:** The applicant is presented as a new card type that **walks on from the left** of the screen. The player either lets it walk off to the right (decline) or hires it (walks into the hand / is employed). Hiring costs **no immediate coins** but adds an ongoing per-turn salary cost (deducted alongside existing staff/community-space ongoing costs during the income phase, clamped at 0 coins).
- **Capacity & let-go economics:** A business can employ one staff member per business level (level 1 = 1 slot, etc.). The player can let a staff member go (lay off), which costs 1 turn's salary and 1 reputation.
- **Tests & docs:** The mechanic is covered by unit tests (deterministic trigger under seeded RNG, passive-buff application, hire/decline, let-go penalties, per-level slot enforcement) and a browser/scene test for the walk-on/walk-off presentation. All related documentation is updated (code comments, README/wiki docs entries as applicable). Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Staff applicants for this mechanic are **distinct** from the existing hand-slot staff cards (`handSlotsAdded` mechanic) — they do not go into the player's hand as hand cards; they are employed at a deployed business.
- Applicant pool starts from existing staff templates; add new applicant cards via the follow-up work item CG-0MT1CIWSD003VBPK (not scope here).
- Passive buffs are applied per-business; must not conflict with existing per-slot `currentIncome` / `currentReputationPerTurn` caching in `applyIncome`.
- New card presentation must follow SLL positioning and the shared HandView/PileView / animation + SFX conventions per AGENTS.md (rule 8, `COMMON_SFX_KEYS`, reduced-motion respected).

## Existing state

- `StaffCard` interface in `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` (familly: 'staff') with `handSlotsAdded`, `reputationPerTurn`, `refreshCostDiscount`, `actionsPerTurn`. Staff templates loaded from `card-data.csv` (`_STAFF_CARD_TEMPLATES`).
- `MainStreetState.ts`: `streetGrid` of deployed businesses/community-spaces; `staffCards[]` (hand-slot staff) + `staffCardMarket[]`; business cards carry `maxLevel`/`level`.
- `MainStreetEngine.ts`: `hireStaffCard()` (hand-slot hire), `layOffStaffCard()` (hand-slot layoff), `executeDayStart()` resets per-turn state; `applyIncome()` in `MainStreetAdjacency.ts` deducts staff + community-space ongoing costs and applies per-slot income/rep.
- Related peek skill work: CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN (implement staff peek skill), CG-0MSXOWLHU0099QF6 (face-down deck rendering).

## Desired change

Introduce a per-turn staff-applicant phase/step in the turn loop: roll the applicant chance, when triggered pick a deployed business with a free employment slot and spawn an applicant card that walks on from the left. On hire, employ the applicant at that business, add its passive specialization buff to the business's income/rep/synergy computations, and register its ongoing salary cost. On decline, walk the card off to the right with no effect. Add per-level employment-slot tracking, and a let-go action costing 1 turn's salary + 1 reputation.

**Key Files:**

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — new state: applicant presentation state, per-business employment slots, employed-applicant list.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — new applicant-trigger step, hire/decline/let-go actions, ongoing-cost integration; `resolveIncident`-style applicant chance roll.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — apply passive specialization buffs per-business in `applyIncome` (+ currentReputationPerTurn).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — applicant/specialization skill type definitions (start with existing templates + Town Gossip skill).
- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — Town Gossip skill / any new specialization columns if added.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` + `MainStreetAnimator.ts` — new card type walk-on (from left) / walk-off (right) / walk-into-hand animation + SFX.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` / `MainStreetCommands.ts` — hire/decline input + command wiring.
- `tests/main-street/` — unit + browser tests for the mechanic.

## Related work

- CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN — Implement staff peek skill ("Town Gossip" active peek).
- CG-0MSXOXN81004MW8I — Add peek once-per-turn unit tests.
- CG-0MT1CIWSD003VBPK — Staff specialization: new applicant card suggestions (follow-up, out of scope here).
- CG-0MSQJ7VL9009JHF4 — Group F: Staff abilities beyond hand slots.

- Q: Are specializations passive or active? — Answer (producer): Passive, always-on buff applied to the business at which they are employed. Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20.
- Q: When is the specialization randomized? — Answer (producer): Once per game at start, locked for the full game. Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20.

# Income Phase: phased card-effect animations (coin grids, synergy/rep/event contributions)

**Priority: High** | **Type: Feature** | **Marked for producer review**

## Objective

When the turn ends and the IncomePhase resolves, step through all income card effects one at a time, in a phase-based order and pacing that reads clearly to the player. Starting with base income, each affected business/community-space card shows its income coins "counting out" into a coin grid rendered on the card; then synergy, reputation, event, and upcoming-card contributions either fly coins into that grid or (for negative effects) fly coins out. This replaces the current single-fly-to-HUD collection with a legible, per-contribution breakdown.

## Users & User Stories

- **Player** — "When I end my turn I want to *see* where my income came from — how much each business produced on its own, how much came from synergy and reputation, and how much events changed—so the economy feels legible and satisfying."
- **Player (reduced motion)** — "I still want to follow the phases and see the contributed amounts, but without the coin flights."

## Problem statement

End-of-turn income is currently collapsed into a single coin-per-slot that arcs to the HUD counter (CG-0MSRGTUSK003GDGE). The player cannot tell how much came from base income vs synergy vs reputation vs event modifiers, which undermines the "watch your town pay out" moment.

## Desired change

Rework the income-collection presentation into a phase-based, per-card coin-grid animation:

1. **Base income "counts out" of each card** — for each producing business/community-space, the card's base income (rounded to nearest 0.5 after this phase) appears as coins (full coin per whole 0.5; half coin for a remainder) that animate out of the card into a coin **grid rendered on the card**. Coins accumulate on the card across phases.
2. **Synergy coins fly in from the synergy line** — coins from the synergy multiplier fly from the synergy line (shared `synergyLineEndpoints` geometry) into the affected card's grid.
3. **Reputation coins fly in from the HUD** — coins from the reputation multiplier fly from the reputation score HUD into the grid.
4. **Event-card effects** — any event card (active duration effects, e.g. Flu Outbreak 0.8×) that affects income flies coins in (boost) or out (reduction) to/from the affected business cards. Duration effects are indicated via animated text lines (see below); single-turn effects just fly the coins.
5. **Upcoming cards** — upcoming cards that affect income either fly coins in, or fly coins out (from the business to the upcoming card, where they disappear).
6. **Grid-to-HUD collection** — at the end of the income step, the accumulated coins on each card's grid fly to the HUD coins counter (reusing/extending the existing fly-to-HUD + final "+total" pop behaviour).

**Coin grid packing (per user):** start as a 5×3 grid; when space runs out, overlap/shrink the coins to fit 10×3, then 15×3, etc. Exact packing "whatever works well" — 3 rows with columns growing (5/10/15...) and shrinking coin size / overlap as needed.

**Rounding (per user, Q8):** each *phase* rounds its own portion to the nearest 0.5 for the coins shown in the grid. The HUD / credited total still uses the exact fractional value (current behaviour preserved).

**Phasing (per user, Q3):** phase-based — all cards show base alongside, then all cards' synergy, then all cards' reputation, then each event, then upcoming-card effects. Each phase lasts ~2–3 seconds. **Reduced motion keeps the phases (same sequence + pacing) but removes the coin animation** (no flights / count-out tweens); the per-phase rounded values still appear.

**Duration-effect text lines (Upcoming panel):** for event cards with a duration, indicate their effect via an animated text line — on a *new* card the effect text animates in one letter at a time with a grow/shrink animation. Then, for each line (new and pre-existing), coins fly to/from the affected business cards. *(The Upcoming-deck-as-face-down-single-card redesign that frees the panel space is a SEPARATE work item — CG-0MSXIQDI4007K6N0 is unrelated (HUD decimals); the deck redesign has no ID yet and is out of scope here.)* This item assumes the panel already has room for these effect lines; if it does not yet, this item proceeds with the best available placement and the deck redesign is tracked separately.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. End-of-turn income walks through phases in order (base → synergy → reputation → events → upcoming), each ~2–3s, with on-card coin grids that accumulate rounded coins per phase (nearest 0.5 per phase).
2. Base coins "count out" of each producing card into its grid; synergy coins fly in from the synergy line; reputation coins fly in from the reputation HUD; event/upcoming effects fly coins in or out to/from the appropriate cards.
3. Grid packing scales from 5×3 to 10×3 to 15×3 by shrinking/overlapping coins as space requires; overflow is visible, not clipped.
4. At the end, grid coins fly to the HUD coins counter with the existing final "+total" pop and coin-pop SFX (extending CG-0MSRGTUSK003GDGE); the credited HUD total is unchanged (exact fractional total preserved).

# Intake Brief: Main Street — Banking-Aware AI Strategy (Deliberate Action Hoarding)

## Problem Statement

Main Street's AI strategies (GreedyStrategy, RandomStrategy) consume the daily action budget greedily every turn with no concept of action banking. Since action banking (CG-0MT3IOPZB005LNAR) lets unused actions persist across days (capped at 2), the AI never conserves actions — it spends everything and loses the remainder. Banking is therefore a human-only strategic tool. The AI needs a deliberate hoarding strategy that banks actions on some days to enable bigger multi-action plays later (e.g., move-to-hand + buy-and-place combo, premium placement), with look-ahead depth and aggressiveness that scales down at lower difficulties.

## Users

- **Players** of Main Street — they expect the AI opponent to use the same strategic tools humans have, making games feel strategically deep and fair at each difficulty.
- **TCE developers / producers** — need the banking-aware AI to be testable (unit + Monte Carlo), balanceable by difficulty, and cleanly separated from the existing Greedy strategy.

Example user stories:

- "As a player on Medium/Hard, I want the AI to occasionally skip a low-value spend to bank an action for a high-value play I can see coming, so the opponent feels thoughtful."
- "As a player on Easy, I want the AI to under-bank compared to higher difficulties, so difficulty still matters."
- "As a developer, I want a distinct banking-aware strategy I can select in Monte Carlo and tune per difficulty, without risking regression in the existing Greedy baseline."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **New banking-aware strategy (separate from Greedy):** A new `BankingGreedyStrategy` class is added alongside the existing `GreedyStrategy` — Greedy is left unchanged; `RandomStrategy` is unchanged. The new strategy implements `MainStreetAiStrategy` and is selectable by name (e.g. `BankingGreedy` / `banking-greedy`) wherever strategies are chosen.

2. **Deliberate hoarding behaviour:** The new strategy can choose `end-turn` even when `actionsRemaining > 0` when hoarding is higher-value than spending. When the heuristic's expected value of banking exceeds the best immediate spend's value, the AI banks; otherwise it spends normally via the existing Greedy scoring/priority logic.

3. **Hybrid banking heuristic with difficulty-scaled look-ahead (Q1c + Q3 + Q6):** A new scoring function evaluates the value of banking by considering (a) currently visible unaffordable high-value targets — in hand and in the market row — and (b) anticipated near-future targets via look-ahead into the market/deck pipeline. The heuristic factors current `bankedActions`, the target's cost vs. available coins, and the AI planning horizon (`aiPlanningHorizon()` from CG-0MSN1A71G005AF7W). Look-ahead depth / banking aggressiveness is reduced at lower difficulties (e.g., Easy banks rarely / looks only at visible cards, Hard considers deeper look-ahead and banks more aggressively). The exact tuning is documented in code comments and validated by tests.

4. **Bank-cap handling — natural via heuristic (Q4: producer leaves to implementer):** No special-case "always bank" branch; the heuristic naturally handles the cap — at `bankedActions == 2` the value of further banking is zero/negative, so the AI spends. Spending and cap enforcement already come from the engine (Q4 accepted as implementer's call to let the heuristic govern).

5. **Monte Carlo harness integration as a new strategy variant (Q5: new):** The Monte Carlo harness (`MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts`) registers a new strategy name distinct from `greedy` (e.g., `banking-greedy`) so runs can compare baseline Greedy vs. banking-aware. Guardrail tests (`monte-carlo-guardrails.test.ts` or equivalent) stay green within tolerance for the new strategy (or a drift report + baseline update is produced per policy CG-0MT4ZHRP5002QMS2); existing `greedy`/`random` baselines are not silently replaced.

6. **Tests — deterministic banking scenarios:** Unit tests in `tests/main-street/ai-banking-strategy.test.ts` (new) cover, deterministically: (a) the new strategy hoards when a visible high-cost target exists that is currently unaffordable, (b) it spends when no valuable future target justifies hoarding, (c) it does not over-hoard (banks toward cap then spends), (d) it respects action-budget limits and existing legality constraints, (e) difficulty scaling — Easy hoards less than Hard given the same state. Existing `ai-action-budget` and `monte-carlo` tests remain green.

7. **Documentation:** `docs/main-street/` (or equivalent) and in-code comments document the new strategy's existence, when it banks vs. spends, and how difficulty scales look-ahead/aggressiveness. No tutorial changes (Q7: no).

## Constraints

- **Main Street only** — no core-engine changes.
- **Additive strategy:** `GreedyStrategy` and `RandomStrategy` are left unchanged; the banking-aware behaviour lives in a new class so existing behaviour can still be baseline-tested.
- **Bank cap 2, at-most-1 banked per day, day-start composition `1 + gmBonus + min(2, banked)` — all unchanged**; spending / capping comes from the engine. Engine correctly decrements banked on action spend (fix at CG-0MTCP7F9S009HARC).
- **Hybrid heuristic required (Q1c):** consider both immediate visible targets and look-ahead, with look-ahead reduced at lower difficulties (Q1 parenthetical) and overall aggressiveness scaled by difficulty (Q6: yes).
- **Banking-aware strategy is a new Monte Carlo strategy name (Q5):** do not replace the existing `greedy` entry.
- **Tutorial unaffected (Q7: no)** — tutorial coverage for action banking remains the separate item CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P.
- **Prerequisite:** Bank-consumption fix CG-0MTCP7F9S009HARC (in_review) — banking-aware AI builds on its corrected `consumeAction` semantics; track the dependency and adapt if that fix's semantics shift.

## Existing State

- `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — `GreedyStrategy` with an 11-step priority chain (play business/upgrade from hand, buy upgrade, buy business, move-to-hand, buy event, play event, discard, community favour, hire staff, end-turn) and horizon-scored business/upgrade valuators. No banking concept. `RandomStrategy` is budget-oblivious uniform pick. Both respect budget only via `enumerateLegalActions` filtering.
- `MainStreetState.ts` — `bankedActions: number` field (init 0), serialized/deserialized, included in undo/redo snapshots.
- `MainStreetEngine.ts` / `MainStreetCommands.ts` — `executeDayStart` composes `bankedActions` into the day budget; `processEndOfTurn` banks unused actions; engine/command spend paths decrement `bankedActions` (fix at CG-0MTCP7F9S009HARC, in_review).
- `MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — runs `GreedyStrategy` / `RandomStrategy` across seeds and difficulties (`MonteCarloStrategy = 'market-greedy' | 'demo-greedy' | 'greedy' | 'random'`); guardrail tests compare to `docs/main-street/monte-carlo-baseline.json`.
- `aiPlanningHorizon()` (CG-0MSN1A71G005AF7W) — `clamp(ceil((winThreshold - score)/8), 5, 25)` used for scoring business/upgrade income over future turns; available to reuse for banking valuation.
- Tests: `tests/main-street/ai-action-budget.test.ts` validates AI respects the action budget; does not test banking-aware decisions.

## Desired Change

Add a new `BankingGreedyStrategy` that wraps/extends the existing Greedy valuation but first evaluates an implicit "bank actions" option: score the best immediate legal spend vs. score the expected value of banking one action given visible + look-ahead targets and difficulty-scaled look-ahead depth. When banking wins, return `end-turn` early (deliberate hoard); otherwise delegate to the standard Greedy priority chain. Register the new strategy under a distinct name in the Monte Carlo harness so `banking-greedy` can be run and guarded separately from `greedy`.

## Key Files (Predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — Add `BankingGreedyStrategy` (and supporting `scoreBankOption()` / look-ahead helpers); leave `GreedyStrategy` and `RandomStrategy` unchanged; document difficulty scaling in comments.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — Register new `banking-greedy` strategy name (extend `MonteCarloStrategy` union + `ALL_STRATEGIES`, wire `createAiPlayerForStrategy`); keep existing `greedy` path unchanged.
- `tests/main-street/ai-banking-strategy.test.ts` (new) — Deterministic unit tests for (a) hoard vs. spend, (b) no over-hoard to cap-then-spend, (c) budget legality, (d) difficulty-scaled aggressiveness, (e) hybrid visible + look-ahead triggers.
- `tests/main-street/monte-carlo-guardrails.test.ts` (or new guardrail file) — Include/validate the new strategy; drift report + baseline update if intentionally shifted, per CG-0MT4ZHRP5002QMS2 policy.
- `docs/main-street/` — AI behaviour section documenting the new strategy and difficulty scaling.

## Related Work

- **CG-0MT3IOPZB005LNAR** (completed) — Action banking mechanic (state + engine + UI + tests). Prerequisite this builds on.
- **CG-0MTCP7F9S009HARC** (in_review) — Bank consumption fix (decrement banked on action via shared `consumeAction`). Prerequisite for correct banking semantics.
- **CG-0MSX41S7I009MMZN** (completed) — AI & Monte Carlo action budget awareness — existing tests validate AI respects budget.
- **CG-0MSN1A71G005AF7W** (completed) — AI threshold-distance planning horizon (`aiPlanningHorizon`) — reused for banking valuation.
- **CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R** (completed) — Base action economy (`actionsRemaining`, `actionsPerTurn`).
- **CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P** (open) — Tutorial coverage for action banking. Explicitly out of scope here per Q7.
- **CG-0MM4RG1GM0SRVENC** (completed) — PRD Milestone 6 extraction/refactoring (automated find_related match).
- **Automated find_related** at intake start also surfaced repo file matches under `example-games/main-street/` and `tests/main-street/` consistent with the Key Files above; full report sidecar at `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-CG-0MT3JMGA60091J8W.md`.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Monte Carlo baseline drift:** Banking-aware runs may shift win-rate / coin-per-turn. Per CG-0MT4ZHRP5002QMS2 policy produce a drift report and re-baseline only when the shift is intentional (not a hidden regression).
- **Look-ahead complexity:** Hybrid visible + deck look-ahead is more complex than visible-only; scope the look-ahead narrowly (few cards ahead / top of deck) and gate depth by difficulty to keep the strategy testable. If look-ahead proves too noisy, narrow to visible targets with a documented fallback.
- **Over-/under-hoarding:** Too aggressive ⇒ AI seems passive; too timid ⇒ no observable banking. Mitigate with difficulty-scaled thresholds and the four deterministic tests in AC6.
- **Dependency on CG-0MTCP7F9S009HARC:** If the bank-consumption fix's semantics change before it lands, this strategy's valuation must adapt — track the dependency.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Per-difficulty Strategy parameter objects, hint-system integration, or re-tunable economy rebalancing are out of scope — record as linked work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q1 — Banking heuristic trigger: "What determines when the AI should bank vs. spend? (a) visible unaffordable high-value targets, (b) look-ahead at market/deck, (c) hybrid?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-01, this session): "c (where look ahead is reduced at lower difficulty levela)".** Source: interactive reply this session. Research: inspected `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` (Greedy priority chain + `aiPlanningHorizon`), `MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` strategy wiring, and `MainStreetState.ts` banked fields (see context-gathering in prior intake). Resolved: hybrid visible + look-ahead, with reduced look-ahead at lower difficulties.
- Q2 — Strategy granularity: "Parameter on GreedyStrategy, new BankingGreedyStrategy, or modify Greedy in place?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-01): "new".** Source: same session reply. Resolved: additive new class; Greedy and Random left unchanged.
- Q3 — Hoarding depth: "How far ahead should the AI plan; leverage aiPlanningHorizon?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-01): "yes".** Source: same session reply. Resolved: reuse `aiPlanningHorizon()` for banking valuation alongside the new heuristic.
- Q4 — Bank cap interaction: "When already at cap (2), still evaluate banking or handle via heuristic?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-01): "your call".** Source: same session reply. Resolved: implementer's call — heuristic naturally returns zero/negative value at cap so the AI spends; no special-case branch (documented in AC4).
- Q5 — Monte Carlo strategy variant: "New banking-greedy name or replace existing greedy?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-01): "new".** Source: same session reply. Resolved: distinct `banking-greedy` strategy name; existing `greedy`/`random` unchanged.
- Q6 — Difficulty tuning: "Should banking aggressiveness vary by difficulty?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-01): "yes".** Source: same session reply. Resolved: aggressiveness / look-ahead depth scales with difficulty (Easy less aggressive than Hard).
- Q7 — Tutorial: "Does tutorial need to cover banking-aware AI?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-01): "no".** Source: same session reply. Resolved: no tutorial changes; tutorial banking remains CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P.

# Main Street competitive mode: AI opponent on the shared street

## Problem Statement

Main Street is single-player only; the `MainStreetState`, `MainStreetEngine`, and PRD M3 were never designed for an opponent. Players asked for competitive play — racing an AI on the shared street grid — but the engine assumes single ownership of coins, hand, actions, street slots, and score. Adding competitive mode requires splitting those concerns while preserving single-player behaviour and the existing AI/hint/Monte Carlo stack.

## Users & User Stories

- **Player (competitive mode):** As a Main Street player, I want to play against an AI opponent on the same shared street so each turn I have a rival to race and react to.
- **Developer / QA:** As a developer, I want a head-to-head Monte Carlo harness for competitive mode so balance between player and AI can be measured across seeded runs.
- **Future AI iteration:** As an AI developer, I want the AI decision layer ownership-aware and staff-free so competitive strategy is coherent without rewriting the hint/balance harness.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Per-player state & ownership:** A competitive state model exists with per-player coins/reputation, hand, staff, action budget, and score, plus owner-tagged street slots; deterministic and replayable via seeded RNG. Single-player behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] **AC2 — AI plays a legal competitive turn:** The AI generates legal actions through `enumerateLegalActions` (competitive mode) with staff actions excluded, scored by an ownership-aware `scoreAction`/helpers, and executed via `executeAction`. Verified with legality and determinism tests.
- [ ] **AC3 — Per-owner income; shared events:** Income accrues only to the owning player of each placed business; street-wide investment events and incidents retain their existing resolution semantics, routed per-owner as specified. Validated by income/event unit tests.
- [ ] **AC4 — Competitive Monte Carlo harness:** A head-to-head harness (extending `MainStreetMonteCarlo`) runs >=200 seeds and produces win/score distributions plus per-player metrics; single-player AI tests still pass.
- [ ] **AC5 — Engine-only scope confirmed:** PRD M3 is updated to note this deliberate scope extension; competitive mode has no game-selector entry or scene yet — rendering (owner-coloured street, shared-market phase alternation with SFX/animations per AGENTS.md 8) is deferred to a planning-created child.
- [ ] **AC6 — Tests & docs:** Relevant unit tests and new tests cover AC1–AC4; build succeeds; affected docs/comments are updated.
- [ ] **AC7 — Full test suite passes** with the new changes (release gate; not a per-push requirement beyond `npm run build` + unit tests).

## Constraints

- Competitive mode scope is **state + engine + AI + Monte Carlo only** — no game selector entry, no competitive scene, no competitive UI chrome yet (AC5 deferred to a planning child).
- Turn alternation: **alternate MarketPhases within a shared day** (confirmed producer decision). Income/Incident/EndCheck phases are shared once both players have acted. Implementation design stays within planning.
- Win condition: **first player to reach the win threshold wins**; the game offers an endless continuation option beyond threshold (confirmed producer decision). Endless mode wiring is within the parent unless planning creates a dedicated child.
- `MainStreetAiPlayer` / `MainStreetAiStrategy` / `GreedyStrategy` / `scoreAction` / `enumerateLegalActions` are unchanged for single-player consumers.
- Determinism via seeded RNG is preserved; replays remain reproducible.

## Existing State

- Single-player-only state (`MainStreetState` resourceBank/hand/staffCards/actionsRemaining), engine (`applyIncome`, `resolveEvent`, `resolveIncident`, `computeScore`, `checkEndConditions`), PRD M3, and AI layers (`MainStreetAiStrategy`, `GreedyStrategy`, `scoreAction`, `MainStreetAiPlayer`, `MainStreetMonteCarlo`) built for one owner. Reusability findings documented in the original description.
- One child item already exists: **CG-0MT5X3N79002S038 — Competitive AI strategy (ownership-aware, staff-free)**.

## Desired Change

Ship an **engine-level competitive mode**: per-player state + owner-tagged grid, per-owner income routing, shared event semantics, ownership-aware and staff-free AI scoring, and a competitive Monte Carlo harness — without changing single-player behaviour or adding competitive rendering. Record the scope extension in PRD M3 and plan the rendering/scene child for the next milestone.

## Decisions Since Original Item

- **Turn structure:** Option A (alternate MarketPhases within a shared day) confirmed by producer.
- **AC5:** Deferred to planning — will become a child for rendering/selector/scene work.
- **Denial reasoning:** Opponent-aware denial (blocking best slot, buying to deny) intentionally deferred to a follow-up child.
- **Win condition:** First to threshold wins, with an endless continuation option beyond threshold.
- **Owner-coloured street (AC5):** Means tinting each placed business's street slot by owner (e.g., player = blue, AI = red) so the shared grid's ownership is visually unambiguous.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — Split to per-player resources/hand/staff/actions/score; owner-tagged `StreetGrid` slots.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Per-owner income, shared event/incident routing, shared-day phase handling, competitive helpers.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — Ownership-aware `scoreAction`/per-type helpers + competitive `enumerateLegalActions` variant (staff excluded); single-player paths unchanged.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — Competitive head-to-head harness (extension).
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-3.md` — Note competitive mode as deliberate scope extension beyond M3.
- `tests/main-street/*.test.ts` (+ new competitive tests) — Unit + deterministic replay coverage for AC1–AC4; existing guardrails still passing.

## Related Work

- Related work items (from `find_related`): CG-0MM5ZGB8U02S0BFO — Main Street Scenario & Tutorial (completed) · CG-0MOXGGZXJ002X6H3 — [test-failure] MainStreetScene animation scheduling (completed) · CG-0MS9NXIEX00880UV — [test-failure] hud-layer-contract (completed)
- Related docs (from repo scan): `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-3.md` · `docs/DEVELOPER.md` · `AGENTS.md`
- Child: CG-0MT5X3N79002S038 — Competitive AI strategy (existing; align description with this parent's clarified ACs).
- Existing state/engine/AI/monte-carlo layers are the implementation basis (see Existing State above).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **State split regressions in single player:** score/income/event paths silently ignore per-player split. Mitigation: keep single-player API shim and run full single-player regression suite.
- **Income/event routing divergence:** per-owner bugs hard to diagnose. Mitigation: explicit per-owner unit fixtures + deterministic replay across seeds.
- **AI ownership semantics under-tested:** greedy heuristics mis-score denial/synergy when ownership added. Mitigation: head-to-head harness + baseline comparisons (AC4).
- **Phase alternation complexity:** alternating MarketPhases within one day adds state machine edge cases. Mitigation: diagram shared-day phases in planning and cover transitions with unit tests.
- **Scope creep toward rendering:** temptation to start the selector/scene early. Mitigation: AC5 is explicitly deferred; new rendering asks become planning-linked children.

## Open Questions

None — all open intake questions have been answered by the producer (see Comments). Remaining design detail (per-player state shape, phase machine, Monte Carlo metrics schema, endless-mode trigger) is within planning.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q1 (Map, via `wl comment add CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30`): "Alternating turn structure — Option A (alternate MarketPhases within a shared day) vs Option B (alternate full days)?" — Answer (producer, 2026-09-01): "a" → resolved as **Option A** (alternate MarketPhases within a shared day). Recorded in `wl comment` (producer decisions comment).
- Q2 (Map, via `wl comment add CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30`): "Child item coverage for AC5 — create competitive-scene child now or defer to planning?" — Answer (producer): "planning. for now what do you mean by 'owner colored streets'" → resolved as **deferred to planning**; follow-up clarification Q5 added. Recorded in `wl comment`.
- Q3 (Map, via `wl comment add CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30`): "Denial reasoning scope — deferred or minimum viable?" — Answer (producer): "deferred" → denial is **out of scope** for this epic, may become a follow-up child.
- Q4 (Map, via `wl comment add CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30`): "Win condition — first to threshold, fixed days, or simultaneous?" — Answer (producer): "when one player rea hes a win conditiion with option to carry on in endless mode" → **first to threshold wins, with endless continuation option**.
- Q5 (Map, implicit follow-up): "What does 'owner coloured streets' mean?" — Answer purpose: rendering the shared street grid where each placed business slot is visually tinted by owner (e.g., player blue, AI red) so ownership is immediately readable. Scene concern deferred to planning child.

# Intake Brief: Improve Main Street sell-price formula (CG-0MT5XO7DI0066QCT)

## Problem statement

When a player sells a business or community-space card from the street grid, the refund is a flat 50% of purchase cost plus upgrades — it does not reflect the business's actual accumulated value through synergy bonuses. This makes selling underperforming cards unfairly punitive and disconnects the sell price from the economic value the player has built up.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — needs an emergency sell option that fairly reflects the card's current value so they can raise meaningful emergency cash without being unfairly penalized.

**Example user stories:**

- "As a player, when I sell a business that has synergy income/reputation bonuses from its neighbors, I want the sell price to include those bonuses so I recover more of the value I've invested."
- "As a player, I want the sell price formula to be consistent with the buy-and-place premium mechanic, so the game feels balanced."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **New sell-price formula:** The sell refund is calculated as `refund = Math.ceil((card.cost + totalUpgradeCost) * 1.5) + synergyIncomeComponent + synergyReputationComponent`, where:
   - `1.5` is the same +50% buy-and-place premium multiplier used for same-day composite and drag-and-drop placements
   - `totalUpgradeCost` is the sum of all upgrade costs applied to the card (via `totalUpgradeCost` field)
   - `synergyIncomeComponent` = the card's `currentIncome` minus its base income (`baseIncome + incomeBonus + sameTypePenalty`), i.e. the synergy income bonus portion only
   - `synergyReputationComponent` = the card's `currentReputationPerTurn` minus its base reputation (`repPerTurn + repBonus`), i.e. the synergy reputation bonus portion only
   - Both synergy components are added as flat amounts (not multiplied) — matching the component-based approach (Q2: b)

2. **Applies to both business and community-space cards:** The new formula applies to all `BusinessCard` and `CommunitySpaceCard` types on the street grid (matching the existing sell flow — Q3: both).

3. **Sell dialog updated:** The sell confirmation dialog (`showSellConfirmation` in `MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`) displays the new, higher refund amount so the player sees the exact coin value before confirming.

4. **Log entry updated:** The activity log reflects the new formula (e.g., "Sold X for +Y coins" with the new Y value).

5. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

6. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The 1.5× multiplier applies to the **total** of base cost + upgrade cost (Q1: total) — i.e. `1.5 × (card.cost + totalUpgradeCost)`.
- Synergy components use `Math.max(0, ...)` to avoid negative contributions — if same-type penalty reduced income below base, the synergy component does not reduce the refund.
- If `card.currentIncome` or `card.currentReputationPerTurn` is `undefined` (card hasn't been recalculated since placement), treat the respective synergy component as 0. This is a defensive guard; in normal gameplay the card should always have been recalculated before sell eligibility.
- The base income fields (`baseIncome`, `incomeBonus`, `baseSynergyCoinBonus`, `repPerTurn`, `reputationBonus`) are **readonly** on the card — synergy is always `currentIncome - baseTotal` where `baseTotal = baseIncome + incomeBonus + sameTypePenalty`. For cards without upgrade-derived `incomeBonus`, use `card.baseIncome * (hasSameTypePenalty ? 0.6 : 1)` as the base component.
- Synergy components are computed with the card still active (not yet marked sold), so the synergy values reflect the card's current contribution on the grid.
- Rounding: `Math.ceil()` on the base refund component; synergy components are added as whole numbers (they are already integers from `currentIncome`/`currentReputationPerTurn`).
- The sell flow remains unchanged: MarketPhase click → confirmation dialog → sell → card marked sold → slot stays occupied.
- Only the sell price formula changes; all other sell behavior (legality, undo, visual treatment, neighbor recalc) is unchanged.

## Existing state

- **Current formula:** `refund = Math.ceil((card.cost + totalUpgradeCost) / 2)` — 50% of purchase + upgrades, no synergy component.
- **Implementation location:** `sellBusiness()` in `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarket.ts` (line ~1099).
- **Synergy calculation:** `computeBusinessIncome()` in `MainStreetAdjacency.ts` computes `baseIncome + synergy`, where `currentIncome` is the cached total. The synergy portion is `currentIncome - (baseIncome + incomeBonus + sameTypePenalty)`.
- **Reputation calculation:** `computeSingleCardReputation()` returns `repPerTurn + repBonus + synergyRepBonus`.
- **UI:** `showSellConfirmation()` in `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` displays refund amount as text.
- **State fields on cards:** `totalUpgradeCost`, `currentIncome`, `currentReputationPerTurn` are all available on placed card instances.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** `card.currentIncome` and `card.currentReputationPerTurn` are always up-to-date when the player clicks sell. In normal gameplay the card is recalculated on placement, sale, and turn end, so this should hold. The defensive `Math.max(0, ...)` and undefined guard provide safety nets.
- **Risk — formula complexity:** The new formula introduces more terms than the previous flat 50% calculation. Players may find the refund amount unexpected if they don't understand synergies. Mitigation: the sell dialog should display the breakdown (base premium + synergy income + synergy rep) so the player understands the calculation.
- **Risk — same-type penalty edge case:** A card with same-type neighbors has reduced base income (60% of base). The synergy component is `currentIncome - baseTotal` where `baseTotal` already includes the 0.6 penalty. If `baseTotal` is lower than the synergy portion, the refund correctly adds synergy on top of the reduced base. No negative refund risk due to `Math.max(0, ...)`.
- **Risk — scope creep:** The sell dialog enhancement (showing formula breakdown) is a UI detail, not a game mechanic change. If UI polish is deferred, the core formula still applies. Keep the dialog change in scope but make it a secondary priority.
- **Risk — undo/redo:** The undo command captures a snapshot of state before the sell. Since `refund` is a computed value (not stored in state), undo restores the pre-sell state automatically — no changes to undo infrastructure needed.
- **Scope creep risk:** Adding a "sell price breakdown" tooltip to the street grid (hover to see potential refund) is a separate feature opportunity. Record as a potential follow-up work item, not in scope.

## Desired change

1. **Engine:** Replace the refund calculation in `sellBusiness()` with:
   ```
   baseRefund = Math.ceil((card.cost + totalUpgradeCost) * 1.5)
   synergyIncome = card.currentIncome - (baseIncome + incomeBonus + sameTypePenalty)
   synergyRep = card.currentReputationPerTurn - (repPerTurn + repBonus)
   refund = baseRefund + Math.max(0, synergyIncome) + Math.max(0, synergyRep)
   ```
   (Use `Math.max(0, ...)` to avoid negative synergy contributions — if same-type penalty reduced income below base, the synergy component should not reduce the refund below the base.)

2. **UI:** Update `showSellConfirmation()` to display the new refund amount with the formula breakdown (base + synergy components).

3. **Tests:** Unit tests for the new formula edge cases: no upgrades, multiple upgrades, synergy bonus, same-type penalty reducing income, zero synergy cards (e.g., Pawn Shop with `synergyCoinBonus = 0`).

**Key Files:**

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarket.ts` — Update `sellBusiness()` refund calculation (core formula change)
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — Update `showSellConfirmation()` to display new refund
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — Update refund pre-calculation passed to `showSellConfirmation()` (mirrors `sellBusiness` formula)
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — Reference for synergy calculation helpers (read-only)
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — Card type definitions (read-only, confirms `totalUpgradeCost`, `currentIncome`, `currentReputationPerTurn` fields)
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetSellCards.test.ts` — New/updated unit tests for sell formula (add cases: synergy bonus, same-type penalty, zero-synergy card)

**Related work:**

- `CG-0MQOA5U4H000J37N` — "Sell cards in Main Street" (original implementation, completed) — this item improves the sell formula
- `CG-0MT5XT7K3005IBBV` — "Add a close business option to main street" (planned, not started) — parallel feature, not affected

**Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers**

- **Q1 (multiplier scope):** "Should the 1.5x multiplier apply to both the base card cost AND the total upgrade cost (i.e. 1.5 x (card.cost + upgrades)), or only the base card cost?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-01):** apply to the **total** (1.5 x (card.cost + upgrades)). Source: interactive reply. Final: total.
- **Q2 (synergy formula):** "Additive bonus (refund * (1 + synergyBonus)) vs. component-based (refund + synergyIncome + synergyRep)?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-01):** **component-based (b)** — flat add of synergy income + synergy reputation components. Source: interactive reply. Final: b.
- **Q3 (community-space scope):** "Does the new sell-price formula apply to both business and community-space cards, or business cards only?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-01):** **both** families. Source: interactive reply. Final: both.

# Intake Brief: Add a close business option to Main Street (CG-0MT5XT7K3005IBBV)

## Problem statement

In Main Street, a business/community-space card on the street grid can only be **sold**, which refunds 50% of purchase+upgrade cost and leaves the card **permanently on the grid** in an inert "sold" state — the slot stays occupied for the rest of the game (placement requires an empty slot). Players need a **Close** option: an action-consuming, coin-free action that **removes the card from the street entirely**, freeing the slot so a new card can be placed there later.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — wants to replace an underperforming business instead of being stuck with a dead sold card in a key slot.

**Example user stories:**

- "As a player, I want to close a business that is losing money (negative ongoing cost) so I can place a better card in that slot on a later day."
- "As a player, I want to clear a community-space card from the street without keeping it as a permanently occupied slot."
- "As a player, I want a clear, confirmable way to close a street card (costing 1 action, no coins) distinct from selling it (free, refund, stays on the grid)."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Scope & UI (feature behavior):** During `MarketPhase`, every **non-sold** business and community-space card on the street grid offers a **Close** option; **sold** cards never do. The existing click-a-street-card confirmation dialog (`showSellConfirmation`) is extended into a **Manage card** dialog with **[Sell] [Close] [Cancel]** buttons (reusing `createOverlayBackground`/`createOverlayButton`, HUD-container parenting, depth 199/200/201).
2. **Cost:** Closing consumes **exactly one daily action** via the shared `consumeAction` helper (`actionsRemaining` and `bankedActions` decremented, floor 0 — CG-0MTCP7F9S009HARC) and grants **no coins**. Selling remains free and unchanged.
3. **Removal:** Closing removes the card from `streetGrid[slotIndex]` (slot → `null`), pushes it to the `discardPile` (not removed from the game), incrementally updates affected neighbors' cached income/synergy values, writes an activity-log entry, and the slot becomes **immediately placeable** by new cards.
4. **Undo & feedback:** Close is a **reversible command** (`closeBusinessCommand` via the undo manager restores the card, slot occupancy, action budget, and neighbor values) and is rendered with an **animation + SFX** consistent with the existing sell demolition (`animateSell`) and the event-driven audio rule (`COMMON_SFX_KEYS`, reduced-motion respected).
5. **Quality & docs:** Unit tests cover legality (MarketPhase, non-sold, slot occupied, action sufficiency), cost, removal, neighbor recalculation, and undo; a browser test covers the Manage-card dialog (Sell / Close / Cancel); HUD/help tooltips and docs are updated (`core-rules-and-mechanics.md` action-economy table: Close added under *action-consuming* operations, explicitly NOT in the "Free operations" list; GDD action-economy section; `ux-visual-audio.md` if the close animation differs); the **full test suite passes** (`npm test`) and the production build succeeds (`npm run build`).

## Constraints

- Action cost must go through the **single shared `consumeAction`** enforcement point (CG-0MTCP7F9S009HARC) — same path as `buyBusinessCommand`/`buyAndPlaceBusinessCommand`; no double-decrement, no divergence.
- Follow the engine's existing patterns: `LegalityResult` discriminated union (`canCloseBusiness`), reversible `toCommand`/`snapshotAction` command, and `MainStreetMarket` action module structure mirroring `sellBusiness`/`canSellBusiness`.
- Modal dialog must follow the project's UI best practices (backdrop 199, box 200, interactive 201; parent all text/buttons into `hudContainer`; `dismissOverlay` cleanup) and SLL for positioning.
- Event-driven audio rule (CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N-context rule in AGENTS.md): the close action must be animated and sounded via the shared helpers/SoundManager; `shakeIllegalMove`/illegal feedback for rejected closes; reduced-motion and mute/volume settings respected.
- i18n: dialog/label strings should follow the game's i18n pattern if the existing sell dialog strings are localized.
- Doc-update policy: this is a rules/mechanic change — `docs/main-street/*` must be updated in the same change; create a doc-update child work item if it can't land in the same commit.

## Existing state

- **Sell from street:** `sellBusiness` (`MainStreetMarket.ts`) marks `soldSlots[slotIndex] = true`, refunds `Math.ceil((purchasePrice + upgradeCosts) / 2)`, card stays on grid (inert — no income/synergy), **free** (no action consumed). Legality gate `canSellBusiness` (MarketPhase only, unsold only). `updateNeighborsOnSale` recalcs neighbors.
- **UI entry:** clicking a non-sold street card in `MarketPhase` → `MainStreetTurnController.onSellCard` → `MainStreetOverlayContent.showSellConfirmation` (Sell/Cancel, refund text) → `sellBusinessCommand` (free).
- **Placement:** `canPlaceFromHand` requires `streetGrid[slotIndex] === null` — so a sold card permanently occupies its slot today.
- **Engine legacy helper:** `sellFromTableau` already models "remove card entirely + to discard pile", but is unused by the street UI and prices at 75% (old PRD semantics) — NOT to be reused for Close (Close pays nothing).
- **AI:** `enumerateLegalActions` does not enumerate street sells (player-initiated); no AI changes expected, but verify — costs/empty-slot should not break AI budget tests (`ai-action-budget.test.ts`).
- **Docs:** `core-rules-and-mechanics.md` lists "Selling a business" under **Free operations**; Close must be added as an action-consuming op.

## Desired change

Add a **Close** action alongside Sell for street-grid cards: click a non-sold card → Manage card dialog ([Sell] [Close] [Cancel]); Close costs **1 action, no coins**, removes the card from the grid (slot → null), sends it to the discard pile, recalcs neighbors, logs the activity, animates + sounds the removal, and is undoable. Sold cards remain permanently on the grid (unchanged) and are not closeable.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarket.ts` — add `closeBusiness()` + `canCloseBusiness()` (+ `CloseResult`) mirroring the sell helpers; neighbor recalculation (reuse `updateNeighborsOnSale`-style logic)
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCommands.ts` — add `closeBusinessCommand()` (consumes action via shared `consumeAction`; undo snapshot restores card/action/neighbors)
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — extend `showSellConfirmation` into the Manage-card dialog (Sell / Close / Cancel) or add a parallel dialog
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — manage-card entry + close handler (legality, action-cost messaging, tutorial gating parity)
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — street-card click/tooltip wiring (sold cards stay non-interactive; tooltip text)
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetAnimator.ts` — close removal animation + SFX (reuse/parallel `animateSell`)
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — tooltip copy if the free-ops list changes (Close must not appear there)
- `example-games/main-street/i18n/` — localized strings for the new dialog if sell strings are localized
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — verify enumeration/budget unaffected (should be, like street sell)
- Tests: `tests/main-street/CloseBusiness.test.ts` (unit: legality, cost, removal, neighbors, undo) + a browser dialog test (or extend `MainStreetSellCards.test.ts` / `MainStreetPlaceSell.test.ts`)
- Docs: `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (action-economy table), `docs/main-street/the-build-gdd.md` (action economy), `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` (close animation), game help text/README if they describe street-card actions

## Related work

- CG-0MTCP7F9S009HARC — shared `consumeAction` enforcement point (must be reused for Close's action cost)
- CG-0MT24X0SX007RLHN — same-day composite buy-and-place pricing (context for the action economy; Close must not affect it)
- CG-0MSLXJCHH001DLIO — no turn-limit default (close-as-action fits the longer-horizon economy)
- CG-0MQVJ4DIC009K8D8 — Scenario Validation Test (critical; close legality must not break scenario validation)

**Related work (automated report — /skill:find-related):**

- **CG-0MM4RFN5N0KTUR66** — Main Street: PRD Milestone 5 -- Tutorial, Onboarding, and Game Selector Integration (completed; tutorial-gating context for the new dialog)
- **CG-0MSKU0BE5003I2ZD** — Main Street: merge business hand + held event into one horizontal 3-card hand (completed; hand/street interaction context)
- **CG-0MQK7IQE9003LH7X** — panel status lines not working (completed; overlay/panel polish context)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** a closed card goes to the `discardPile` (consistent with `sellFromTableau`); it is not removed from the game, and it never returns to the market.
- **Risk — action economy:** Close is a new way to spend actions (effectively "demolish + refund-free sell" at the cost of 1 action). Monitor for degenerate play patterns (e.g., closing a card then immediately re-buying a better one each day); balance guardrails (`balance-guardrail-recommendations.md`) may need a follow-up review.
- **Risk — scope creep:** AI usage of Close, challenge interactions, tutorial/two-turn-step teaching updates, and stats/transcript schema changes are out of scope for this item — file follow-up work items if discovered during implementation.
- **Risk — sold-slot semantics:** sold cards permanently occupying slots is unchanged by this feature; a future "clear sold card" capability could be a separate work item.
- **Compatibility:** i18n coverage of new strings and browser-test interaction with tutorial gating must be checked; undo of Close must also restore the tutorial step state if gated.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (action cost):** "Does 'costs nothing' mean a free operation (no coins AND no daily action, like sell), or does closing consume a daily action (like placing)?" — Answer (producer, via work-item review): **consume a daily action** (1 action point, no coins). Source: producer reply to intake questions comment, 2026-08-30.
- **Q2 (UI entry point):** "How does the player trigger a close?" — Answer (producer): **as recommended** — extend the existing click-a-street-card confirmation dialog into a Manage card dialog with [Sell] [Close] [Cancel]. Source: producer reply, 2026-08-30.
- **Q3 (scope):** "Does Close apply to both business and community-space cards, and should sold (inert) cards be closeable?" — Answer (producer): **apply to all except sold** — both families are closeable; sold cards are not. Source: producer reply, 2026-08-30.
- **Q4 (discard) — noted assumption, not asked:** closed card → `discardPile` (slot → null, placeable). Open to revision if the producer prefers removal from the game.

`MainStreetMonteCarlo` is single-player only (`runMonteCarlo` / `runAllCombinations` with one strategy × one difficulty per run). Competitive mode needs head-to-head metrics: both players' win/score distributions plus per-player diagnostics. ## Scope

- Single-player AI tests (`ai-strategy.test.ts`, balance guardrails) still pass unchanged.

- AI strategy itself (sibling).
- Per-owner income routing (sibling).
